area: THE HOST BRIDGE: WHAT IS TRUE TODAY (LabConstrictor-Tools, napari-labconstrictor, LabConstrictor-Fiji, LabConstrictor-QuPath, and the apps that declare tools)

facts.statement: The bridge does not use an 'installer registers the application' step in the generic sense; a post-install hook in the app's installer runs `python -m labconstrictor_tools register ...`, which writes a JSON entry plus a cached schema into a per-user registry folder (~/.labconstrictor/apps, override LC_HOME; also LC_APPS_PATH and a system folder). Hosts read that folder.
facts.evidence: LabConstrictor-Tools/docs/LABCONSTRICTOR_INTEGRATION.md steps 1-5 and 'Where the registry is'; labconstrictor_tools/registry.py:1-14 (docstring: 'one <name>.json entry plus a cached <name>.schema.json per app ... Written by an app's post-install step'). Playground app/bash_bat_scripts/post_install.sh:85-101 shows the real hook.

facts.statement: The hook only acts if the app ships a module named exactly <package>_lc_tools; apps without it are unaffected. The hook also pip-installs labconstrictor-tools from a GitHub zip (not on PyPI) at install time, so the user's computer needs internet then; failure never fails the installation.
facts.evidence: LABCONSTRICTOR_INTEGRATION.md 'What an app must contain' and step 3; docs/AUTHORING.md 'Naming rule'; Playground post_install.sh:85-90 default LC_TOOLS_SPEC=https://github.com/CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-Tools/archive/refs/heads/main.zip. PyPI JSON for labconstrictor-tools, napari-labconstrictor, labconstrictor-fiji all returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-11.

findings:
CORRECTED 6-STEP ARCHITECTURE (replaces the spec's list)
1. An app declares tools. The app author writes typed Python functions with @tool in a module named <package>_lc_tools (NucleiSky: src/nucleisky_lc_tools, tool 'Relocalize 2D'; heavy imports go inside the function). The declaration is turned into a JSON schema (protocol: 1) WITHOUT running the tool.
2. The app installer (its post_install.sh/.bat hook, not an operating-system registration) finds <package>_lc_tools in the app's own Python, pip-installs the small standard-library-only labconstrictor-tools package (from a GitHub zip, since it is not on PyPI), and runs `labconstrictor_tools register`. That writes <name>.json and a cached <name>.schema.json into ~/.labconstrictor/apps (LC_HOME / LC_APPS_PATH / a system folder also searched). Entries are trust-checked (owner, not world-writable, interpreter inside its prefix, protocol supported) and skipped with a visible reason otherwise. The uninstall hook runs `unregister`. Caveat: this hook lives on the template's unmerged `bridge-test` branch; apps must copy it (Playground and GuessTheCondition did, NucleiSky only on its bridge-test branch).
3. The user installs a host plugin separately (napari plugin pip-installed from GitHub; Fiji jar or Groovy script; QuPath jar). Two separate installs: app and plugin.
4. The host reads the cached schemas (no Python subprocess and no scientific imports at discovery; 'Rescan apps' in napari re-reads the registry) and generates its own form: napari dock widget with magicgui fields and group headings, 'Show advanced settings', greyed EnabledWhen; Fiji a SciJava dialog with '— Group —' headings (no greying); QuPath a JavaFX window. Image inputs offer an open layer/window/image or a file ('or file' / '(or file)').
5. On Run the host starts a separate worker process with the APP'S OWN Python interpreter (`python -m labconstrictor_tools serve --module <package>_lc_tools`), speaking an Appose-compatible JSON-lines protocol (LAUNCH, UPDATE progress, COMPLETION/FAILURE/CANCELATION). The host exports images as TIFF (or shared memory) and never imports the app's packages, so apps with conflicting dependencies coexist. Cancel is cooperative; a tool that ignores it is killed after 3 s. napari can keep the worker alive between runs; Fiji starts a new one each run (about 12 s for NucleiSky).
6. Typed outputs return to the host: images/labels become napari layers / Fiji windows / QuPath preview; affine alignment becomes an overlay (napari layer 'NucleiSky:alignment', magenta additive, opacity 0.8; Fiji window 'Alignment overlay (green = reference, magenta = query)'); points become points layer / point ROIs / point annotations; shapes become shapes layer / overlay+ROI Manager / annotations; tables become a table dock / Results table; scalars go to the status line (napari) or Log (Fiji); messages to a quoted block or dialog. Every run is also logged (~/.labconstrictor/logs/labconstrictor.log, runs/<time>_<app>_<tool>/run.json) and 'Copy as command' reproduces it on the command line.

MATURITY (verbatim anchors for the page)
- READMEs: 'Status: testing phase'. Linux only for real apps (napari 0.9 under Xvfb; Fiji with Java 21 under Xvfb). Windows only under Wine; the .bat install hooks have never run on real Windows; macOS untested. QuPath is titled '(prototype)'.
- Guides (what a visitor reads): 'Under heavy construction ... untested and unlikely to be stable.' Host project status: Experimental. No releases, no PyPI, no napari hub, no Fiji update site. Version 0.1.0 everywhere.
- CI (green on main) covers Python unit/protocol suites on Linux/Windows/macOS and a small napari viewer subset with the example app; Fiji and QuPath GUI tests are manual. The nightly round-trip run failed on all 3 OS in both runs. So Windows/macOS evidence is unit-test level, not real-app level.
- The only real-app end-to-end evidence is one AI-agent walk-through (CLEAN_TEST_REPORT_2026-10-06.md) on Linux with virtual displays, verdict 'Not yet'.

OVERSTATEMENTS / ERRORS IN THE SPECS
1. 'napari/Fiji ... via installer registration' for NucleiSky: no released NucleiSky installer registers anything; the tool exists only on a branch. A demo cannot honestly say 'install NucleiSky and open it in napari'. The honest statement is a prototype on an unmerged branch.
2. Spec 5 step 2 'installer registers the application' needs the corrected wording above (a registry file written by an installer hook that exists only where the app author copied it from the template's bridge-test branch).
3. Idea B 'Playground declares the Feature tour tool for hosts' is true; 'Playground NOTEBOOK has no Feature tour cell' is true.
4. Spec 3B napari: 'App selector NucleiSky' is an unlabelled dropdown; 'Cancel, Rescan apps, Restart worker, Details' are real; add 'Copy as command' only if the newer UI is mocked (it is not in N2/N5).
5. Spec 3C Fiji: app and tool are chosen in preceding small dialogs; Fiji has no Rescan/Restart worker/Details.
6. Spec 14 / fixture values: display the measured result (12.1721, scale 1.0024 physical, 429 reference nuclei, 9 query nuclei, matcher quad) or label a ground-truth number 'illustrative'; do not show 'scale 2' as the NucleiSky result. The 2D_QC.jpg is a separate NucleiSky result (it exists at docs/assets/2D_QC.jpg on NucleiSky main).
7. Spec 6 'repos report Linux testing with actual applications': true only for the AI-agent virtual-display run; no real desktop, no human run recorded.
8. Spec 6 'link ... docs/user-guide.md as the authority': fine, but those guides themselves say 'untested and unlikely to be stable', which is stronger than 'experimental preview'. The spec's tab label 'Experimental integration preview - not yet validated on all operating systems' understates; accurate would be 'Prototype, tested on Linux only'.
9. Site: hubs.yaml alt texts call the screenshot 'a test app'; it is NucleiSky Relocalize 2D from a branch.
10. Stale text: three workflow headers say 'First run still pending' though CI has run 100+ times; HOST_FEATURES.md:30 contradicts its table.
risks: Promoting NucleiSky in napari/Fiji on the website would show something users cannot reproduce from any NucleiSky release or from main; the tool lives only on branch bridge-test (28 commits ahead of main) and the manifest says hosts: [notebook].

Host guides state 'untested and unlikely to be stable'; a polished, faithful demo of napari/Fiji could signal maturity the plugins do not have. Labelling must be 'prototype, Linux-tested' not 'experimental preview'.
Windows and macOS install hooks have never run on real systems; a visitor on those systems who follows the install route may fail, and the website would be the first point of contact.

No plugin is published anywhere (no releases, PyPI, napari hub, Fiji update site); install requires pip from GitHub zips, Maven+Java for Fiji, JDK 25 for QuPath. The install instructions can change without notice (main-branch zips, not versions).
The tools package is installed at app-install time from a main.zip on GitHub, so behaviour can change under a user between installs; no pinning.

Screenshots N2/N5 reflect an older tool form and an odd 1089x1008 window with a PyQt5 deprecation toast; reproducing them pixel-faithfully copies artefacts and an outdated interface; the real current form is longer (Cellpose, Fine-tuning, region fields).
Nightly round-trip tests fail on all three OS and the Fiji macro recorder is known broken (D3); claims about macro/recording or 'tested on every OS' would be false.

Napari and Fiji differ visibly (napari greys EnabledWhen fields, Fiji does not; Fiji has chooser dialogs; Fiji runs ~12 s per run with a fresh worker); a demo that makes them look identical misrepresents the bridge.
Facts verified on 2026-10-11 can move quickly: repos are merged daily (last merges 2026-10-10).
recommendations: Describe the bridge on the site with the corrected 6 steps and the exact words 'prototype', 'testing phase' and 'Linux only so far' (use the READMEs' own status sentences), linking to the four docs/user-guide.md guides and the Playground 0.0.1 release as the route that works today.

If the demo uses NucleiSky in napari/Fiji, label it 'Prototype on NucleiSky's bridge-test branch, not yet in a NucleiSky release' and use measured values (12.1721 deg, 429/9 nuclei, quad, 12 s) rather than ground-truth numbers; keep the fixture from LabConstrictor-Tools/fixtures/make_nucleisky.py (confirmed to exist) and the real screenshots N2/N5/F2/F3 as references.

If a truthful 'try it yourself' route is wanted in the demo, prefer LabConstrictor Playground 'Feature tour' (or 'Check everything'), which really ships in a release with the hook, declares hosts [notebook, napari, fiji, qupath], and has a built-in 256x256 demo image with 16 blobs at defaults; note its notebook has no Feature tour cell, so a three-interface identical view needs a notebook change in another repo.

Reflect in the demo: napari = one dock with two unlabeled dropdowns, 'Run', Cancel/Rescan apps/Restart worker/Details; Fiji = chooser dialogs then a SciJava dialog with OK/Cancel and results in image windows + Log. Do not give Fiji napari's buttons.

Do not claim 'the installer registers the application' without the qualifier; say 'an app that declares tools registers them when installed (a registry file on your computer), then the plugin finds them'.

Fix before publishing (upstream, separately): stale 'First run still pending' workflow comments, HOST_FEATURES.md:30, the site's 'a test app' alt text, and decide whether the guide warning and the 'Experimental' status badges should say the same thing.

Re-check at publish time: NucleiSky bridge-test merge status, template bridge-test merge, any plugin release/PyPI/update-site publication, and the nightly CI state, since these decide whether 'soon' can become 'available'.
